deep.reconstruction:
Page 18 is a combinatorial bookkeeping sheet. It sits between the preceding page, on the nerve/realisation adjunction φ_! ⊣ φ^* between a presheaf category A^ and a topos 𝒳, and Grothendieck's general interest in finite-set-indexed data in 'topos stratifié'.

Objects. 𝔼_n is the standard finite set with n elements. There are two kinds of generating maps:
- ∂_n : 𝔼_n → 𝔼_{n+1}, the inclusion adding one point;
- k_{n-1} : 𝔼_n → 𝔼_{n-1}, the surjection identifying two points.

The top of the page considers spans of epimorphisms I ↠ J, I ↠ K with card ≤ 3 and their pushouts, including iterated ones (I→J→J', K→·→·). It considers the coproduct-type square I ↪ I⊔K → I'⊔K. It also considers the dual diagrams for a contravariant functor X on finite sets: X(I) ← X(I⊔K), X(I') ← X(I'⊔K'), and truncated sequences X_0 ← X_1 ← X_2 mapping to X'_0 ← X'_1 ← X'_2. The product condition X(I⊔K) ≅ X(I)×X(K) is written and then crossed out, replaced by the requirement that such squares be cartesian.

Five elementary types of commutative (pushout) squares are listed:
- I: the coproduct cospan 𝔼_p → 𝔼_{p+q} ← 𝔼_q, with p,q ≥ 1.
- II: two different one-point inclusions of 𝔼_n into 𝔼_{n+1}, completed to 𝔼_{n+2}, n ≥ 1.
- III: an inclusion ∂ and a collapse k on the same 𝔼_n, completed to 𝔼_n, n ≥ 2.
- IV: two collapses k, k' of 𝔼_n whose collapsed pairs share a point, completed to 𝔼_{n-2}, n ≥ 3.
- V: two collapses k, k'' collapsing disjoint pairs, completed to 𝔼_{n-2}, n ≥ 4.

The two tables count how many squares of each type occur when all cardinalities are bounded.
- Card ≤ 3: type I has 2 (p=q=1 and p=1,q=2); II has 1 (n=1); III has 1 (n=2); IV has 1 (n=3); V has 0.
- New squares at card 4 (table I'): type I has 2 (p=1,q=3 and p=2,q=2); II, III, IV and V have 1 each (n=2, 3, 4, 4 respectively).

The distinction between IV (n≥3) and V (n≥4) is confirmed by the counts: disjoint pairs first appear at card 4. So the evident aim is to find a finite generating set of 'exactness' squares. A functor X : (finite sets, card ≤ N)^op → 𝒳 sending these squares to cartesian squares should be determined by X(𝔼_1). In that case X(I) ≅ X_1^I, with the diagonal square X^2 ← X_1, X_1 = X_1 sketched at the bottom right. Equivalently: which truncation level (3 or 4) suffices, and which squares must be checked.

The heavily scribbled-out block is an abandoned attempt to draw these diagrams with 𝔼^2 → 𝔼^1.
errors: No outright errors are visible. The counts are consistent with the interpretation (types II and III at a given n produce sets of card n+2 and n respectively; type V needs 4 points).
Whether squares of types II–V actually generate all pushouts among sets of card ≤ N is not argued on the page. The claim is only implicit.

ideas.what: Presentation of the category of finite sets by inclusions ∂ and collapses k, with elementary commutation/pushout squares sorted into five types
ideas.modern_name: Generators and relations for FinSet (analogue of simplicial identities for Γ/FinSet)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore; cf. presentations of Δ and FinSet (Mac Lane, Segal, Pirashvili)

ideas.what: A contravariant functor on finite sets sending these squares (coproduct, diagonal) to cartesian squares is determined by its value on the one-point set, X(I) = X_1^I; question of which cardinality truncation (≤3 or ≤4) suffices
ideas.modern_name: Product-preserving / finite-limit-preserving functors from FinSet^op (Lawvere theory of sets); truncated Segal-type conditions

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine combinatorial check: listing and counting elementary pushout squares of small finite sets, to fix a truncation level for exactness conditions. Nothing here appears to go beyond standard facts about finite sets and functors on them.
transcription_corrections: The epimorphism arrows are labelled 'épi' (twice) on the page; the card ≤ 3 condition applies to I, J, K.
In the first table, type I reads 'p=q=1 ; p=1(?), q=2' with count 2. The second entry may be read 'p=φ', but p=1 is meant.
In table I' (bottom), V is 'n=4' with count 1. The machine transcription is correct here; note that types IV and V both start at n=4 at this level.
In diagram IV (n≥3) the vertical left map is k'_{n-1}; in V (n≥4) it is k''_{n-1}. Their top arrows are k_{n-1} (one is overwritten). Bottom arrows go 𝔼_{n-1} → 𝔼_{n-2}.
In the second large diagram on the left, the bottom-right entry is J' = I' ⊔ K. On the right, the crossed-out 'X(I)×X(K)' is replaced by X(I⊔K), with X(I'⊔K') below.
